_why: The host documents concise preferred presentation forms while these vectors retain the full renderer and file-opening behavior, including supported forms the prompt does not recommend. Changes here update prompt documentation only; renderer inputs and expectations remain unchanged.

_consumers.renderer: frontend/src/chat/file-citation-prompt-vectors.test.ts runs each documented form through renderMarkdownHtml, the file-citation contract and the chip open path, so a form the prompt promises but the renderer does not honor fails the frontend gate.
_consumers.promptText: tests/reply-prompt-contract.test.ts checks preferred prompt examples with the real file-citation parser, verifies each documentedBy span, and keeps client-only directives out of the shared engine base prompt.

citationForms.name: an absolute-path markdown link renders as a chip
#L12 lands on the chip as a line
#L12-L20 keeps both ends
citationForms.note: A range renders, but the click path consumes only the start line, so the prompt documents no range form.

citationForms.name: the label may differ from the path
a non-numeric fragment is not a location
angle brackets carry a path with spaces
%20 is an accepted equivalent of a space
angle brackets carry an unmatched parenthesis
a comma needs no escaping
citationForms.note: Measured, not documented: an earlier prompt revision claimed commas cut the link grammar short, which is false. Kept so the claim cannot come back.

citationForms.name: balanced parentheses need no angle brackets
a Windows path is a citation too
the explicit directive renders the same chip
the directive survives an unmatched parenthesis
citationForms.documentedBy: If a path cannot be expressed as a Markdown link

brokenForms.name: an unmatched parenthesis without brackets truncates the path
brokenForms.documentedBy: Wrap a destination containing spaces or unmatched parentheses in angle brackets
